title: bug: a missing migration TOOL is reported as a missing migration FILE, and the deploy receipt redacts it
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-08 at HEAD 7622a2e8 by worker-bcaa6d5e from the epic-final row task-99f364e3. Cost me roughly forty minutes to diagnose; it will cost the next operator more, because in production the cause is not visible at all.

WHAT HAPPENS. Deploy a freshly scaffolded (or freshly cloned) product whose workspace has not been installed. The deploy REFUSES. `report.detail` is `DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED` and the receipt's own refusal detail is `[REDACTED]` under the fail-closed policy from task-c78140e9. Probing the migrate port directly is the only way to see the real answer:
  {"code":"MIGRATION_FAILED","detail":"MIGRATION_FILE_UNKNOWN","layer":"DAEMON_INGRESS"}

THE CAUSE, symbol by symbol. `apps/daemon/src/repository/migrations/migration-ports.ts:54 apply` runs `node --input-type=module --eval MIGRATE` with cwd = the deploy's build context. `MIGRATE`'s first statement is `import { runner } from 'node-pg-migrate'` — a WORKSPACE dependency of the generated product. A tree that has never been installed has no `node_modules`, the import throws before `readdirSync('migrations')` is ever reached, no `MOE_MIGRATION_RESULT=` line is emitted, and `:64` throws `new MigrationExecutionError(null)` whose `file` field defaults to the literal `MIGRATION_FILE_UNKNOWN`. So a MISSING TOOL is reported as an UNKNOWN FILE.

THE CONSTANT FOR THE RIGHT ANSWER ALREADY EXISTS AND IS NEVER RAISED FROM THIS PATH: `controlled-profile-generator.ts:43 MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING`, whose own comment says "Defined here for the verifier and deployment migration consumers (children 2 and 3); THEY detect and raise it". Nothing on the deploy migration path does.

CONFIRMED NOT A PATH DEFECT: with the workspace installed, the same tree migrates green and the pipeline completes end to end (task-99f364e3 step 3). The migrations do live at `packages/api/migrations/` while the runner reads `migrations` at the workspace root — that is correct, because `node-pg-migrate` is invoked through the workspace and resolves its own directory; it is NOT the cause here and should not be "fixed".

DEFINITION OF DONE
1. A deploy against an uninstalled workspace refuses with `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING`, distinguishable from a genuinely absent or unreadable migration file.
2. The distinction survives the redaction policy: an operator reading only the receipt can tell "your workspace is not installed" from "your migration file is broken" without a debugger. Redaction must not be weakened to achieve this — the code carries the meaning, not free text.
3. Arms for BOTH conditions: an uninstalled workspace, and an installed workspace with an unreadable migration.
4. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` EXIT 0 with its count line quoted.
definitionOfDone: A deploy whose workspace has no installed migration tool refuses with MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING rather than MIGRATION_FILE_UNKNOWN, and the two conditions are distinguishable from the refusal code alone.
The distinction is readable by an operator from the receipt under the existing fail-closed redaction policy; redaction is not weakened and no free text carries the meaning.
Both conditions have arms: an uninstalled workspace and an installed workspace with an unreadable migration file.
pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test EXIT 0 with its Test Files count line quoted.

implementationPlan.description:
CONFIRM THE CHAIN SYMBOL BY SYMBOL, AND READ THE TWO LINES THAT DECIDE THE DESIGN. NO EDITS.

THE CAUSE (migration-ports.ts): the `MIGRATE` eval script's FIRST statement is a TOP-LEVEL `import { runner } from 'node-pg-migrate'`, which is outside the try at :38. On an uninstalled workspace it throws at module evaluation, so no `MOE_MIGRATION_RESULT=` line is ever written. `apply` then finds no line, `JSON.parse(… ?? "null")` yields null, and :64 throws `new MigrationExecutionError(null)`. The constructor at :14 is `this.file = migrationFilename(file) ? file : "MIGRATION_FILE_UNKNOWN"`. migration-service.ts:69 turns that into `migrationRefusal("MIGRATION_FAILED", error.file)`. A missing TOOL has become an unknown FILE. Confirm each hop by reading.

THE TWO LINES THAT DECIDE EVERYTHING, both in deploy-service.ts:
- `:305-312` — the deploy refuses `DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED @ DAEMON_DEPLOY_ENGINE` and carries the MIGRATION's own `code@layer` in the DETAIL. Its comment says the authoritative code and layer are on the migration receipt, and that a `MIGRATION_*` code cannot BE a deploy refusal code.
- `:167-168` — that detail is `` `${code}@${layer}` `` when the migration detail is empty, and `` `${code}@${layer}: ${detail}` `` when it is not.
So whether the operator can read the answer off the DEPLOY receipt depends on whether the composed string is a pure constant or carries a free-text tail. deploy-ledger.ts:39-46 `PUBLIC_PHASE_DETAILS` is EXACT-membership (no trim, no prefix, no case folding) and its comment at :36-38 says why: `"<phase>: <tool output>"` is exactly how a secret rides beside a safe word.

MEASURE ONE THING THE PLAN BRANCHES ON: whether migration-receipt.ts:74's `text(v.refusal.detail)` accepts an EMPTY string. If it does, the tool-missing refusal can carry `detail: ""` and the deploy detail composes to the bare `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING@DAEMON_INGRESS`. If it does not, use the existing idiom at :24 where `migrationError` passes the CODE as its own detail, composing `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING@DAEMON_INGRESS: MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING` — also a pure production constant with no free text. Record which, and the exact literal you will allowlist in step 4.

CONFIRM THE CONSTANT EXISTS AND IS UNRAISED: controlled-profile-generator.ts:43 exports `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING`, and its comment says the deployment migration consumer is supposed to detect and raise it. `git grep -n MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING` returns only its definition, its type union, controlled-profile-generator.test.ts:157-158 and repository-bootstrap-read.ts:18 with its test at :177 — no raise site anywhere. Confirm that census yourself.
implementationPlan.note: Read live chain and census (git grep -n MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING; source-only results match plan; metadata mentions omitted from note). Top-level import escapes catch -> absent marker -> null -> MigrationExecutionError.file sentinel -> MIGRATION_FAILED. text requires length > 0, so use detail MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING; exact public composite MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING@DAEMON_INGRESS: MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING. Plain MIGRATION_FAILED@DAEMON_INGRESS can remain public only without filename tail. No new layer/command kind. Foreign dirt includes deploy-service.ts and other paths; preserved, no edits there. Loaded explore-before-assume and TDD skills via local files (no Skill tool exposed), read prior Serena task handoff.

implementationPlan.description:
DETECT THE MISSING TOOL WHERE IT ACTUALLY FAILS — INSIDE THE CHILD (migration-ports.ts).

The import cannot be caught where it is. Move `node-pg-migrate` to a DYNAMIC import INSIDE the existing try (`const { runner } = await import('node-pg-migrate')` — the script already runs under `--input-type=module` and already uses top-level await at :39, so this needs no new capability), and emit a result the parent can tell apart. Keep the emitted shape EXACT-KEYED and small; add one field that means "the tool was not importable", do not overload `file` with a sentinel — overloading `file` is the defect this row exists to remove.

DISTINGUISH THE TOOL'S ABSENCE FROM ITS FAILURE. `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for `node-pg-migrate` means the workspace is not installed. Any OTHER error out of the import — a syntax error in the installed package, a native binding that will not load — is NOT a missing tool and must keep its current path. Match on the error's `code` property, never on the message text: Node's wording is not a stable interface, and a message match is exactly the free-text dependence DoD 2 forbids.

THEN CARRY IT UP THROUGH `apply`. `MigrationExecutionError` today carries only `file`. Give the parent a way to say WHICH condition it saw — a distinct error type, or a field on the existing one. Whichever you pick, the four existing construction sites must keep working unchanged: deploy-service.test.ts:823, migration-observation.test.ts:170, goal-deployment-read.test.ts:107 and migration-service.test.ts:124 all call `new MigrationExecutionError("<filename>")` positionally.

DO NOT TOUCH THE MIGRATIONS DIRECTORY RESOLUTION. The filing is explicit: migrations live at `packages/api/migrations/` while the runner reads `migrations` at the workspace root, and that is CORRECT because `node-pg-migrate` is invoked through the workspace and resolves its own directory. It is not the cause and must not be "fixed" — with the workspace installed the same tree migrates green end to end.

RAISE THE CODE THAT ALREADY EXISTS (migration-receipt.ts roster + migration-service.ts mapping).

(1) ADD `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING: "DAEMON_INGRESS"` to the frozen `codeLayers` roster at migration-receipt.ts:12-19. DAEMON_INGRESS is an EXISTING layer and the constant's own comment at controlled-profile-generator.ts:40 says its refusal uses that layer — so this introduces NO new `*_LAYER` constant. That matters right now: a concurrent row (task-44c0178b) has the security lane red over two new `*_LAYER` constants landing without their roster entries. Do not add a layer here; reuse this one.

IMPORT THE CONSTANT, DO NOT RETYPE THE STRING. controlled-profile-generator.ts:43 already exports `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING`, and its comment says the deployment migration consumer is the one meant to raise it. A second literal spelling of the same code is the drift this codebase avoids elsewhere by exporting `MIGRATION_RECEIPT_COMMAND_KIND` for exactly the same reason (migration-receipt.ts:7-10).

DECODING COMES FREE, but verify it rather than assuming: migration-receipt.ts:73 gates on `Object.hasOwn(codeLayers, v.refusal.code)` and :74 on the layer matching, so a receipt carrying the new code decodes once the roster holds it. Confirm a round-trip.

(2) MAP IT AT THE RAISE SITE. migration-service.ts:69 currently produces `migrationRefusal("MIGRATION_FAILED", error.file)` for every failure. Branch on the condition step 2 propagates and produce `migrationRefusal(MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING, …)` with the detail form step 1 measured — empty if `text("")` admits it, otherwise the code itself, following the existing `migrationError` idiom at migration-receipt.ts:24. The detail must be a PRODUCTION CONSTANT either way; the whole point is that no free text carries the meaning.

EVERY OTHER FAILURE KEEPS ITS CURRENT CODE. This row narrows one condition out of `MIGRATION_FAILED`; it does not re-classify the rest.

MAKE THE ANSWER SURVIVE REDACTION WITHOUT WEAKENING IT (DoD 2) — deploy-ledger.ts.

THE PROBLEM, precisely: deploy-service.ts:305-312 puts the migration's `code@layer` in the DEPLOY refusal's DETAIL, and `declassifyRefusal` (deploy-ledger.ts:50-54) replaces any detail that is not an EXACT member of `PUBLIC_PHASE_DETAILS` with `[REDACTED]`. That is why the operator sees nothing today. Step 3 alone fixes the MIGRATION receipt but not the DEPLOY receipt.

THE FIX: add the exact composed literal(s) step 1 measured to `PUBLIC_PHASE_DETAILS`. This is USING the mechanism as designed, not weakening it. That set's own criterion (:31-36) is "every string below is minted by production code with no caller text in it", and a `code@layer` pair drawn from two closed rosters is exactly that — no filename, no stderr, no connection string, nothing an attacker or a tool can steer.

ADD AT MOST WHAT DoD 1 REQUIRES: the two conditions must be distinguishable, so the tool-missing literal and the plain migration-failure literal. Do NOT add a bare `MIGRATION_FILE_UNKNOWN` or any composite carrying a FILENAME tail — a migration filename is caller-influenced text and belongs on the migration receipt, which is not declassified, not in the allowlist.

THE LINE YOU MUST NOT CROSS, and a governor has already ruled on it for a sibling row: `PUBLIC_PHASE_DETAILS` may only ever contain strings minted by production code. Adding a tool-output-derived string there — anything with an `: <detail>` tail whose detail is not itself a constant — would reopen the leak task-c78140e9 closed. If the literal you are about to add is not a pure constant end to end, stop: the fix belongs in step 3's detail choice, not here.

ADD AN ARM FOR THE POLICY ITSELF, in the same file's existing test surface: the new literal survives `declassifyRefusal` verbatim, AND a composite carrying a filename tail is still redacted. The second half is what proves the allowlist did not become a blanket.

BOTH CONDITIONS GET ARMS, AND THEY MUST BE ABLE TO FAIL DIFFERENTLY (DoD 3).

DoD 3 names two conditions and they are not symmetric — write both, and write the second one first if you want the first to mean anything.

(a) AN UNINSTALLED WORKSPACE refuses `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING`. This one needs a real tree with no `node_modules`, because the whole defect lives in a child process's module resolution — a mocked port cannot exercise it and an arm that mocks it proves nothing. migration-real.test.ts is the neighbour that already drives the real path; follow its gating and its cleanup rather than inventing a second harness.

(b) AN INSTALLED WORKSPACE WITH AN UNREADABLE MIGRATION FILE still refuses `MIGRATION_FAILED` carrying the filename. This is the arm that stops (a) from being achieved by making everything report TOOL_MISSING — the failure mode a one-sided fix would ship.

ASSERT THE CODE AND THE LAYER, NOT MERELY THAT IT REFUSED (project rail 1). Two refusal layers can answer here — the migration engine and the deploy engine — so pin WHICH one answered and with which code. A test asserting only "it refused" is one added layer away from vacuous, and this row exists precisely because two different causes were collapsing into one answer.

AND ASSERT THE OPERATOR'S VIEW, which is the row's actual promise: from the DEPLOY receipt alone, after declassification, the two conditions read differently. That is DoD 2's clause and it is not implied by the migration receipt being correct — they are two different records and only one of them is redacted.

Existing arms that must stay green as written: migration-service.test.ts:124, migration-observation.test.ts:170, goal-deployment-read.test.ts:107 and deploy-service.test.ts:823 all construct `MigrationExecutionError` with a filename and expect today's behaviour for a genuine file failure.

ONE CONCENTRATED CLOSE: DRILLS, GATE, ADVERSARIAL PASS (DoD 4).

DRILLS — `git status --porcelain` the mutated paths FIRST; all are TRACKED, so an empty `git diff -- <path>` is a valid restore proof taken in a call SEPARATE from the restore.
(i) THE ROW'S SUBJECT: revert step 2's dynamic import to the top-level one and confirm arm (a) goes RED reporting the old `MIGRATION_FILE_UNKNOWN`. If it stays green, the arm is not exercising real module resolution and (a) is mocked when it must not be.
(ii) THE REDACTION HALF: remove the new literal from `PUBLIC_PHASE_DETAILS` and confirm the operator-view assertion from step 5 goes RED with `[REDACTED]`. That proves the deploy-receipt clause is actually tested, not just the migration receipt.
(iii) THE ONE-SIDED-FIX GUARD: make the tool-missing branch fire for every failure and confirm arm (b) goes RED. That is the regression a rushed version of this fix would ship.

GATE: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, FOREGROUND and STANDALONE, exit code AND the `Test Files N passed` count line quoted verbatim — DoD 4 names it. Read the OUTPUT, not the exit code: a `--filter` leg prints "No projects matched the filters" and EXITS 0. Also run `pnpm typecheck`, since this row changes a roster type (`MigrationCode`) that other modules consume.
This leg is long and has an intermittent history on this host. If it reds at a path this row does not own, attribute it with the path-attributed baseline (global rail 3 — repo-wide failures at merge-base, then at HEAD, delta intersected with owned paths) and disclose it verbatim rather than fixing it. Note in particular that a peer row (task-44c0178b) currently has the SECURITY lane red over unrostered `*_LAYER` constants; this row adds none, so if you see that red it is not yours — say so with the path.

ADVERSARIAL PASS (load `adversarial-self-review`). Ask, in order: what does a workspace with a PARTIALLY installed `node_modules` report — tool missing, or something worse? Does the verifier path (the other consumer the constant's comment names) still report its own way, or did this change reach it? Can a migration filename now leak into the deploy detail through the new branch? And the question the filing itself poses: after this change, can an operator reading ONLY the deploy receipt tell "your workspace is not installed" from "your migration file is broken" — without a debugger, and without any free text having carried the meaning?

**FINDING 1 — THERE ARE TWO RECEIPTS AND ONLY ONE IS REDACTED. This is the trap.** deploy-service.ts:305-312 refuses `DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED @ DAEMON_DEPLOY_ENGINE` and carries the MIGRATION's `code@layer` in the DEPLOY refusal's **detail** — and `declassifyRefusal` (deploy-ledger.ts:50-54) replaces any detail that is not an EXACT member of `PUBLIC_PHASE_DETAILS` with `[REDACTED]`. So raising the new code fixes the MIGRATION receipt (never declassified) and does NOT fix the operator's view. A worker who stops after the raise site will have satisfied DoD 1 and not DoD 2, with everything green. Step 4 handles it; drill (ii) proves it.

**FINDING 2 — THE DETAIL COMPOSITION DECIDES WHAT CAN BE ALLOWLISTED.** deploy-service.ts:167-168 composes `` `${code}@${layer}` `` when the migration detail is EMPTY and `` `${code}@${layer}: ${detail}` `` when it is not. `PUBLIC_PHASE_DETAILS` membership is EXACT (no trim, no prefix, no case folding) and its comment at :36-38 says why: `"<phase>: <tool output>"` is exactly how a secret rides beside a safe word. So the tool-missing refusal must compose to a PURE CONSTANT. Step 1 measures the one branch point: whether migration-receipt.ts:74's `text(v.refusal.detail)` admits an empty string. If yes → `detail: ""` → bare `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING@DAEMON_INGRESS`. If no → pass the code as its own detail, the existing idiom at migration-receipt.ts:24 → `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING@DAEMON_INGRESS: MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING`. And adding a `code@layer` composite to the allowlist is USING that mechanism as designed, not weakening it: the set's own criterion is "minted by production code with no caller text in it", and a pair drawn from two closed rosters is exactly that. What the plan forbids: adding `MIGRATION_FILE_UNKNOWN` or any composite with a FILENAME tail — a migration filename is caller-influenced text and belongs on the migration receipt, which is not declassified. This row adds none, so that red is not this row's.

THE ONE-SIDED FIX IS THE LIKELIEST BAD OUTCOME: make everything report `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING` and DoD 1's first half passes while a genuine broken migration file becomes unreportable. SIX FILES, ONE OVER GUIDANCE, and I did not split.
